title: Livestock production intensity and mucosal IgA and IgG responses to H5N1 highly pathogenic avian influenza A virus, North Carolina, 2021-2022

title: Molecular Surveillance and Nanopore Sequencing Reveal the Circulation and Genetic Diversity of Low-Pathogenic Avian Influenza A Viruses in Migratory Birds from Ukraine

analysis.methods: Influenza A virus detection was performed using real-time RT-PCR targeting the matrix gene, followed by H5/H7 subtype screening. It highlights the utility of portable nanopore sequencing and integrated One Health approaches for monitoring viral diversity and early detection of emerging influenza threats.

analysis.summary_en: This study conducted molecular surveillance of low-pathogenic avian influenza A viruses in migratory birds from Ukraine between October 2025 and January 2026, collecting 604 samples from wild birds and domestic poultry. Using real-time RT-PCR, H5/H7 screening, and Oxford Nanopore sequencing of hemagglutinin genes, the authors detected influenza A virus RNA in 4.97% of samples, identifying H1, H4, and H6 subtypes that clustered within Eurasian lineages. No H5 or H7 subtypes were detected, and domestic poultry samples were negative for influenza A virus. The findings establish a genomic baseline for avian influenza surveillance in Ukraine and demonstrate the value of nanopore sequencing and One Health surveillance for monitoring viral diversity and early threat detection.

analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpreted these findings as proof of concept for direct detection of economically significant avian pathogens in field settings, establishing a foundation for ongoing studies with paired sample testing against validated laboratory reference assays. analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These assays could enable faster, more accessible surveillance and outbreak response for AIV and NDV in poultry, reducing turnaround times and logistical constraints associated with traditional PCR workflows.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study provides analytical validation but does not report clinical sensitivity or specificity in field conditions, pooled sample performance, or combined testing outcomes, limiting generalisability to real-world settings. analysis.summary_en: This study validated direct swab testing for avian influenza virus (AIV) and Newcastle disease virus (NDV) using a closed-tube direct real-time reverse transcription PCR (RRT-PCR) platform. Primer and probe sets were designed using globally circulating sequences to ensure broad genotype coverage. Analytical performance showed high sensitivity and specificity, with successful detection at single-digit genome copy numbers and reliable performance in the presence of cloacal and oropharyngeal matrix material. title: Newton Divided Difference Optimization for Fingerprint-Based Neural Virtual Screening against Avian Influenza A/H9N2

analysis.methods: An aligned benchmark of 1,459 molecules consisting of 615 candidate active compounds and 844 decoys was represented by EState (79 features), PubChem (881 features), and Klekota–Roth (4,860 features) fingerprints, sharing identical molecule identities, labels, and split assignments.
analysis.main_results: NDD achieved the highest descriptive ROC-AUC and PR-AUC on Klekota–Roth fingerprints under scaffold-key and similarity-cluster protocols, and remained competitive under the stratified split with ROC-AUC of 0.9872.

title: Investigating host intracellular proteins with antiviral activity against influenza and herpesviruses

analysis.research_question_and_background: Human pathogenic viruses remain a persistent global public health threat due to endemic infections, seasonal epidemics, and emerging pandemics. Host restriction factors constitute a critical component of innate antiviral immunity that can inhibit diverse DNA and RNA viruses at multiple stages of their replication cycles.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The thesis investigated two host restriction factors, SAMHD1 and MARCHF8, using human and bovine cell models relevant to viral pathogenesis. Studies focused on respiratory RNA viruses, herpesviruses, and bovine herpesvirus type 1 (BHV-1) in macrophage-like, epithelial, neuronal, astrocytic, and keratinocyte cell types.
analysis.methods: Inducible overexpression systems were used to express human and bovine SAMHD1 in relevant cell lines, enabling assessment of antiviral activity against influenza A virus (IAV), human metapneumovirus (HMPV), human parainfluenza virus type 3 (hPIV3), herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1), and BHV-1. Functional assays examined viral genomic replication, late gene expression, and restriction mechanisms.
analysis.main_results: Endogenous SAMHD1 did not restrict seasonal IAV, HMPV, or hPIV3 replication in macrophage-like or epithelial cells, but overexpression inhibited highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) in macrophage-like cells. Endogenous SAMHD1 restricted HSV-1 replication only in differentiated THP-1 macrophages, while overexpression restricted HSV-1 in neuronal but not keratinocyte or astrocytic cell lines. Both human and bovine SAMHD1 restricted BHV-1 replication, with dNTPase activity required for restriction. MARCHF8 restricted HSV-1 replication by inhibiting genomic replication and late gene expression, independent of SAMHD1, CD81, and cGAS-STING pathways.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: These findings demonstrate that SAMHD1 and MARCHF8 act as broad-spectrum host restriction factors across distinct viral classes via mechanisms distinct from those previously described. The study reports the first evidence of MARCHF8-mediated restriction of a DNA virus and identifies cell-type-dependent antiviral activity of SAMHD1.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results highlight the potential of host-directed antiviral strategies targeting SAMHD1 and MARCHF8 to combat diverse viral infections. They also suggest that bovine SAMHD1 could inform control measures for BHV-1, a pathogen with significant economic impact in cattle.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to in vitro cell models and does not address in vivo efficacy or clinical relevance. The strength of evidence is moderate due to reliance on overexpression systems and absence of animal model validation.

analysis.summary_en: This thesis investigated the antiviral activity of host restriction factors SAMHD1 and MARCHF8 against influenza and herpesviruses. Using human and bovine cell models, the study found that endogenous SAMHD1 did not restrict seasonal influenza A virus, human metapneumovirus, or human parainfluenza virus type 3, but overexpression inhibited highly pathogenic avian influenza A(H5N1) in macrophages. SAMHD1 restricted herpes simplex virus type 1 (HSV-1) replication only in macrophages and neurons under overexpression, while both human and bovine SAMHD1 restricted bovine herpesvirus type 1 (BHV-1) replication via dNTPase activity. MARCHF8 restricted HSV-1 by inhibiting genomic replication and late gene expression, representing the first report of its activity against a DNA virus. The findings suggest broad-spectrum antiviral potential for SAMHD1 and MARCHF8 and identify cell-type-dependent restriction mechanisms.

title: Understanding moral trade-offs in pandemic response: A discrete choice experiment on avian influenza policies

analysis.research_question_and_background: Pandemic preparedness requires navigating trade-offs between health, economic, and social impacts; choices that often involve moral tensions.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This study investigates how the Dutch public evaluates such trade-offs in the context of a potential outbreak of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI).
analysis.methods: Using a discrete choice experiment (DCE) administered to a representative sample of 1,045 respondents from the LISS panel, we examined preferences across six policy outcomes: mortality, lasting physical and mental injuries, postponed healthcare, social restrictions, and one-off tax payments.
analysis.main_results: A latent class logit model identified four distinct preference profiles, revealing substantial heterogeneity in moral and economic reasoning.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: Two classes exhibited taboo trade-off aversion (TTOA) when values such as life or human dignity were traded against monetary costs.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Respondents displaying TTOA emphasized solidarity and governmental responsibility, while cost-sensitive groups prioritized economic efficiency.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: These findings highlight that public acceptance of pandemic policies depends not only on effectiveness and cost but also on perceived moral legitimacy.

analysis.summary_en: This study explores how the Dutch public evaluates moral trade-offs in pandemic response policies related to avian influenza. Using a discrete choice experiment with 1,045 respondents, the research identifies varying preferences across six policy outcomes, including mortality, injuries, healthcare delays, social restrictions, and tax payments. The analysis reveals four distinct preference profiles, highlighting substantial differences in moral and economic reasoning. Two groups showed aversion to trading values like life or human dignity for monetary costs, emphasizing solidarity and governmental responsibility, while others prioritized economic efficiency. The findings suggest that public acceptance of pandemic policies depends on perceived moral legitimacy, not just effectiveness and cost. The study's results underscore the importance of incorporating moral considerations into economic evaluations for improved societal acceptability of future pandemic preparedness strategies. However, the study is limited to examining preferences through a survey method, which may not fully capture real-world decision-making processes.

title: Generation of Nasal Cell-Derived Human Alveolar Organoids and Organoid-Macrophage Assembloids for in Vitro Lung Modeling.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed nasal cell-derived human alveolar organoids and alveolar macrophages from peripheral blood monocytes, then co-cultured them into organoid-macrophage assembloids that exhibited enhanced maturation and dynamic epithelial-macrophage interactions. Influenza virus infection experiments demonstrated differential replicative fitness between H5N1 and H1N1 viruses that recapitulated authentic in vivo tropism. Notably, the addition of alveolar macrophages reduced infection by both H5N1 and H1N1 viruses, suggesting a protective effect against viral dissemination. The authors propose these models as universally accessible and physiologically relevant in vitro platforms for biomedical research and translational medicine.

title: Detection of circovirus and herpesvirus co-infection in suddenly dead

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addressed the sudden death of six common ravens (Corvus corax) by investigating potential viral and toxic causes, as the underlying aetiology remained unclear despite the birds being in good nutritional condition.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Six common ravens found dead on the same day in central Poland were subjected to necropsy, with samples collected for bacteriological, histopathological, toxicological, and molecular examinations to identify pathogens and toxins.
analysis.methods: Necropsies included bacteriological, histopathological, and toxicological analyses, while molecular methods screened for circoviruses, herpesviruses, flaviviruses, adenoviruses, polyomavirus, avian bornavirus, avian paramyxovirus-1, rotavirus, avian reovirus, avian influenza viruses, Chlamydia spp., Salmonella spp., Clostridium spp., and botulin toxins.

analysis.summary_en: This case report investigated the sudden death of six common ravens in central Poland through comprehensive necropsy, histopathological, toxicological, and molecular analyses. Histopathological findings included multifocal hemorrhages, inflammatory infiltrates in the liver, intranuclear inclusion bodies in hepatocytes, renal inflammation, degeneration, and necrosis, alongside mild intestinal inflammation. The authors suspected raven herpesvirus as the primary cause of death, reported for the first time in this species, though other factors such as poisoning or unknown pathogens could not be ruled out. The study underscores the importance of targeted surveillance for herpesvirus and circovirus in corvids for wildlife health and potential zoonotic risk assessment.

title: The complexity of protecting poultry from HPAIV: Findings from a case-control study in Sweden.

analysis.research_question_and_background: High pathogenicity avian influenza (HPAI) has caused severe disruptions to poultry production in Sweden and globally over the last decade, creating a need to identify farm-level risk factors to guide prevention measures.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A case-control study was conducted in southern Sweden, including 15 HPAI outbreak farms from 2020–2021 and 33 control farms across four poultry categories and three counties.
analysis.methods: Data were collected via farmer/farmworker interviews and on-farm observations using a questionnaire and the Biocheck.UGentTM tool, with predictor variables selected from a hypothesised causal diagram and analysed using stability selection based on three regularisation models.
analysis.main_results: The case-control analysis identified an association between HPAI outbreaks and the presence of waterfowl near poultry farms, while the cross-sectional study found that turkey farms had higher outbreak risk and broiler farms had lower risk.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study highlights waterfowl proximity as a key risk factor for HPAI outbreaks in Swedish poultry, with poultry category (turkeys vs. broilers) also influencing risk, suggesting targeted biosecurity measures may be needed.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform targeted surveillance and biosecurity interventions in Swedish poultry farms, particularly in regions with high waterfowl activity or turkey production.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study did not find significant associations with biosecurity scores or other covariates, and trends identified require further research, limiting the strength of evidence for actionable conclusions.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated farm-level risk factors for highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) outbreaks in Swedish poultry during 2020–2021 using a case-control design comparing 15 outbreak farms to 33 controls across four poultry categories and three counties. Data were collected through farmer interviews and on-farm observations using a structured questionnaire and the Biocheck.UGentTM tool, with risk factors analysed via stability selection models. The main findings showed that proximity to waterfowl and poultry category (higher risk in turkeys, lower in broilers) were associated with HPAI outbreaks. While the study did not identify significant associations with biosecurity scores, it suggests that targeted surveillance and biosecurity measures in high-risk settings, particularly near waterfowl habitats or turkey farms, may help mitigate future outbreaks.

title: Development of a Visual Rapid Assay for Novel Goose Astrovirus Detection Based on RT-MIRA -PfAgo

analysis.research_question_and_background: Goose astrovirus genotype 2 (GAstV-2) causes gosling gout, a disease requiring rapid detection for early diagnosis and field surveillance, yet conventional methods are time-consuming and require specialized equipment.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study developed a visual assay for GAstV-2 detection using one-step reverse transcription multienzyme isothermal rapid amplification (MIRA) combined with Pyrococcus furiosus Argonaute (PfAgo) nucleic acid cleavage activity.
analysis.methods: MIRA primers and guide DNAs were designed targeting a conserved region of the GAstV-2 ORF1b gene, and PfAgo reaction conditions were optimized with 1.0 μM gDNA, 0.6 μM PfAgo, and 1.0 mM MnCl2.
analysis.main_results: The assay detected as few as 1.0 × 100 copies/μL of recombinant plasmid DNA template and showed no cross-reactivity with GAstV-1, Tembusu virus, H9-subtype avian influenza virus, goose circovirus, fowl adenovirus serotype 4, or goose parvovirus.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The RT-MIRA-PfAgo assay provided sensitive and specific GAstV-2 detection without thermal cycling or expensive real-time PCR instruments, representing a novel visual detection method suitable for basic laboratories and field settings.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: This method may enable rapid, low-cost GAstV-2 detection for early diagnosis and surveillance in resource-limited settings, potentially improving outbreak control and reducing economic losses in waterfowl farming.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to preliminary evaluation with 23 clinical samples and plasmid DNA, lacking large-scale validation, clinical performance metrics, and assessment of field robustness, warranting moderate confidence.

analysis.summary_en: This study developed a visual rapid assay for Goose astrovirus genotype 2 (GAstV-2) detection by combining one-step reverse transcription multienzyme isothermal rapid amplification (MIRA) with Pyrococcus furiosus Argonaute (PfAgo) cleavage activity. The assay targets a conserved region of the GAstV-2 ORF1b gene and operates under optimized conditions with 1.0 μM gDNA, 0.6 μM PfAgo, and 1.0 mM MnCl2. It achieved a detection limit of 1.0 × 100 copies/μL plasmid DNA and demonstrated specificity with no cross-reactivity against GAstV-1, Tembusu virus, H9-subtype avian influenza virus, goose circovirus, fowl adenovirus serotype 4, or goose parvovirus. In a preliminary evaluation of 23 clinical samples, results were concordant with conventional RT-PCR and RT-qPCR. The method eliminates the need for thermal cycling and expensive instruments, offering a rapid, low-cost alternative for GAstV-2 detection in basic laboratories and field settings.
